title: Siemens, ex-Jackson, MS, city directors join 10 others subpoenaed in $89.8M settlement probe - NewsBreak
text: The Siemens Corporation and four former Jackson public works directors have been subpoenaed by U.S. District Judge Henry Wingate as he expands his probe into the city’s $89.8 million water settlement. The new order, filed Tuesday, July 22, mirrors a set of subpoenas Wingate issued earlier this month to 10 other groups — including city departments, law firms and JXN Water — with nearly identical language and demands for bank records, contracts, invoices and internal communications. The only changes are the names of those targeted, addresses and updated dates. Those now facing subpoenas include as they appear on the order: City Attorney Drew Martin told Wingate at a July 14 status conference that Jackson is in the process of compiling records tied to the Siemens settlement. Martin said roughly $30 million went to legal fees, while most of the remaining $59.8 million was spent by September 2020 on bond debts, water and sewer deficits and other expenses. It remains unclear whether the other subpoenaed groups have responded. Siemens, which refunded Jackson $89.8 million in 2020, was not part of the initial 10 subpoenas Wingate issued on July 9. Wingate has signaled that a complete accounting of how the settlement was handled is essential before he considers JXN Water’s proposed water rate hike. Back in June during a public hearing in Wingate's court over a proposed water rate increase for Jackson residents, Wingate shifted focus to the Siemens settlement, asking Henifin where the money went. Henifin told Wingate that about 33% of the settlement — slightly over $29 million — went to the attorneys representing the city. That left around $60 million for Jackson’s use. Henifin also said he believed some of it was used to pay overdue water and sewer bills, but the rest couldn’t be accounted for. Wingate then directed Henifin to investigate. Just over three weeks later, Wingate sent out the first batch of subpoenas. Jackson’s lawsuit against Siemens alleged the company and its subcontractors failed to deliver a working water billing system under a contract awarded in 2012, leaving residents with faulty meters, uncollectable accounts and massive financial shortfalls. In 2019, then-Mayor Chokwe Antar Lumumba announced the city was suing Siemens for the botched work. Siemens, which denied wrongdoing, agreed to a $89.8 million settlement in 2020 to to resolve the dispute and city officials said the refund would help stabilize Jackson’s water finances. The legal dispute and settlement all took place during former Lumumba’s administration. Lumumba has not been named in either subpoenas and left office June 30. The two subpoenas suggest the federal government is examining whether any of those settlement funds were misused or improperly reported. According to the orders, officials are particularly interested in whether the city used the money for debt repayment, infrastructure repairs, capital projects or any other financial obligations. Both command production of any documents “relating to the approximately $89.8 million settlement between the City of Jackson, Mississippi, and Siemens Industry, Inc.,” and notes that recipients must provide any records in their “possession, custody, or control, or otherwise accessible.” The subpoenas gives recipients 30 days to produce the documents. If the city or other parties fail to comply, they could face sanctions or further court orders compelling the release of records. And both warn: "Noncompliance may result in contempt proceedings." Charlie Drape is the Jackson beat reporter. You can contact him at cdrape@gannett.com. This article originally appeared on Mississippi Clarion Ledger: Siemens, ex-Jackson, MS, city directors join 10 others subpoenaed in $89.8M settlement probe
